missionPremise: A fresh planner with no stake in the Texas scale-up scope rev 3 attacks ten named theses, verdicts each as HOLDS / HOLDS WITH A NAMED CONDITION / DOES NOT SURVIVE with a file+SHA or query+timestamp, names a second mechanism that would produce the same observation, launches no sub-agents, writes no product code and no store, and files the review plus a ranked must-change list before a single build row is allocated.
completionPredicate: All ten theses carried a verdict; every verdict cites a file at a pinned SHA (five SHAs pinned: doc_repo 288aa9eb, hauska-factory 9171279, hauska-map 88ac6c51, legacy-design-tools 0bf2377f, hauska-engine 422c7d3a); each thesis carries a second mechanism; T6 names classes with no executable check; the falsifiers are scored; four artifacts are committed to seat/dispatch-planner and pushed. Verdict tally: 6 DOES NOT SURVIVE, 4 HOLDS WITH A NAMED CONDITION, 0 HOLDS unconditionally.

falsifier: FIRED on falsifier 1: six of ten theses do not survive (T1 Phase 0 exit, T2 P-201 zero-earned gate, T6 blocker register as pre-bake checklist, T7 Phase 0 order, T8 defect ownership, T10 missing items), four hold only with named conditions (T3, T4, T5, T9), and none holds unconditionally. FIRED on falsifier 2: T6 names TWO classes with NO executable check in any stage -- C7 (a label asserted by a constant, 46 instances union) and C14 (stranded or unreviewed artifacts, 16 instances) -- and reports that 18 of the 19 class labels have zero executable checks today, the single executable check (six-county-completeness.mjs, covering C13) being hardcoded to the six counties and therefore unusable on Burnet. SATISFIED PARTIALLY on falsifier 3, and the unsatisfied half is a finding: every verdict cites a file at a pinned SHA, but NO verdict cites a query of my own, because FACTORY_DATABASE_URL_RO and ATOMS_DATABASE_URL are both UNSET in this session (psql present, NEON_API_KEY set and deliberately unused). The one quantity I measured myself (T2) was measured by EXECUTING the production modules against a synthetic full-shaped all-unaccounted county, and the transcript is quoted verbatim in the review.
contradicted: TWO LOAD-BEARING CLAIMS IN THE PLAN DO NOT SURVIVE. (1) The program preamble states P-201 must be 'proven by violation on an instantiated, unfilled county' and scope Rev 3 item 1 asserts that a county whose cells exist but are all unaccounted 'still passes evaluatePublishGate'. P-201 HAS landed (factory origin/main 9171279, 'excluded is three states wearing one word') and I executed it: an instantiated, unfilled county returns evaluatePublishGate ok:true with unaccountedCount:0 and 65/65 rails in excludedDeclaredAhead, and evaluateRailGate returns ok:true per rail with verdictKind excluded-not-applicable -- the bucket the new classifier documents as legitimately not applicable. The county is not merely tolerated, it is LABELLED as excluded-for-good-reason. The narrower thing P-201 does (countyGradeSummary/isCountyFullyGraded go false when the (c)-class count is non-zero) satisfies P-201'S OWN ROW CARD but not law 2, and it is satisfied incidentally by rails that have no writer anywhere in Texas rather than by this county's emptiness. Separately and more seriously: evaluatePublishGate and assertPublishableCounty have NO PRODUCTION CALLER at 9171279 -- the sole reference outside their export line is a self-test in parcel-record-fill.mjs -- and the actual publish refusal is requirePreBakeReadiness, whose rail half tests only row.verdict === 'refuse' so that every P-201 value clears. Three things are called 'the gate' and the law names the one on no path. (2) Scope section 4.2's named risk for P-249 ('P-216 took the map down with a one-branch change here') and section 13 item 1 ('The P-216 outage was a one-branch change with map-wide effect') are REFUTED by _inbox/2026-09-15_HANDOFF_planner_snapshot.md's own SUPERSEDED block at the same SHA, which states 'P-216 suppressed the envelope MAP-WIDE is NOT SUPPORTED' and attributes the symptom to a stale operator tab ('A rollback restores the server; it does not reload an open tab'). The register already carries the corrected diagnosis as a candidate class. Also contradicted: the scope's section 16 exit sentence ('Phase 0 exits when this command exits 0') against section 5's four-part exit; section 4.2's R5, which depends on R1 that the same table defers to after Phase 2; section 4.2's R8, whose done-when requires roads/parcelGeometry/edgeSignal to pass in all six counties while the policy table accepts them as excluded; Rev 3 item 5's 'five' quarantined branches against A-181's six; and the register's C15 count of 3 against A-176/scope C7's six duplicate amendment ids.
leave_behind: The plan's law names the wrong gate. Restating law 2 as: publish refusal = requirePreBakeReadiness (population + evaluatePreBakeReadiness over PUBLISH_FLOOR_RAIL_KEYS); reporting surface = evaluateRailGate -> parcel_gate_verdict; evaluatePublishGate/assertPublishableCounty = vendored, no production caller. And restate P-201's done-when as a REFUSAL for a rail that is live program-wide and has zero earned cells in this county, with the violation fixture asserting a refusal rather than a boolean.

P-249's wiring instruction must name depthWarmPromotion: 'depth-warm-promoted-v1' (string marker, with the sourceCitation.includes('depth-warm-verified') fallback and its precedence stated), NOT depthWarmPromoted. Four independent predicates decide 'verified' across three repos (hauska-map atom-chain-to-facets.ts:116/190; the L-B instrument's SQL at envelope-draw-gap.mjs:190 and its in-memory boolean at :122/:226; LDT reconcileAtomEnvelope.ts:51/148 isMachineVerifyDiagnostic) with no divergence test between any pair. Implementing the sentence literally produces a field hauska-map's isDepthWarmPromoted never reads, so LDT's reconciliation and the map's decline compute different answers about the same atom.

P-249's 131,357 is an UPPER BOUND, not an unlock count. scripts/envelope-draw-gap.mjs defines the GAP bucket on the single rail setbackFrontFt (kind='value') joined to atoms entity_type='buildable-envelope' on body->>'parcelNodeId'; the row's predicate requires a district AND a table and the instrument reads neither. Adding 'the unlock count is reconciled to the 131,357 baseline' therefore asks a correct implementation to report a shortfall against a number it must not be measured against. Add the district-and-table-qualified count as a second number.

P-249's declared proof instrument cannot see the failure it exists to catch. The L-B instrument reads two stores and never the serving surface; it would have been GREEN on every side of the 2026-09-15 incident, because the cells were never the problem. The proof needs: a build-identity read by asset EXISTSENCE (never the Age:/Etag header -- A-157 documents Age: as a false instrument shared across alias and rollback target), a fresh browser context per measurement, per-branch assertions on status/declineReason/envelopeCovered/geojson for three branches (unverified zero on a districted, tabled parcel must DRAW; verified zero must stay empty with a named reason; validation-failed must decline with its own reason), a served-payload assertion that no area figure appears without a verified atom, and a rollback rehearsal.

R5 is unreachable in Phase 0 as written. Section 4.2 lists R5 as item 3 of the Phase 0 order with Depends 'R1 to R4, S6' while item 5 of the same list defers R1 and R2 to the road-node pass after Phase 2 (A-177). The re-derive that reaches Waco, Austin and the 123,706 reason-less zeros cannot start. R8 has the same shape: done-when 'All three pass in all six counties' with instrument six-county-completeness, Depends R3, and deferred by the same list while the policy table accepts roads/edgeSignal as excluded. One acceptance standard per row.

S1's flip is not safe on every surface, and the evidence is on file as two unit-test names. hauska-map pe-record-cell-interpret.ts:168 renders unaccounted as an explicit refusal; LDT agValuationFactFromParcelRecord.ts:104 and cityLimitsFactFromParcelRecord.test.ts:89 refuse or render unmeasured; LDT pe-r1-brief-flood.test.ts:414 falls through to the atoms path. But cadRollFactFromParcelRecord.ts:57-60 ('refused cells (unaccounted, engine-refused, store-not-configured, etc.) fall back to null -- the caller keeps the legacy value') and :118 ('anything other than a present coercible dollar (absent, refused, not-applicable, unaccounted, malformed) defaults to stratmap-redistributed') mean S1 applied to the four dollar rails converts an honest absence into a legacy value served under a fabricated basis label. S1 needs a rail allowlist, and section 13 item 1's own instruction to check the surfaces before the flip has already been satisfied -- the answer is in the tests.

There is NO cost telemetry anywhere in hauska-factory. A grep of src at 9171279 for cost_usd/costUsd/estimated_cost/cpu_ms/gb_seconds returns only PROPERTY dollar values, and publish_runs' CREATE TABLE carries only body jsonb plus created_at/completed_at. Law 5 has no column, no table and no writer; commitment 3's kill test cannot fire; and 'Bell and Milam beat Burnet' cannot be a query, which means Rev 3 item 4's promise to decide Bell and Milam's storage FROM Burnet's measured stage records cannot be kept. This is a migration, not a format.

The blocker register cannot be the pre-bake audit's checklist as it stands: 2 class labels (C7, C14 -- 62 instances) have no stage and no check anywhere; 16 more have a check that is prose ('a new script', 'a CI check on the audit-instrument repo path wherever ... live'), 0 of them built; the ONE executable check is county-hardcoded to six counties and so cannot run on Burnet; and the class vocabulary is open-ended (18 declared classes against 55 candidate keys carrying 58 instances, one of them a compound label 'C1/C8' and one counted twice with a note). A checklist needs a closed set. Coverage with denominator: 18 of 19 labels have zero executable checks today.

Phase 0's exit is written twice and the looser version is the actionable one. Section 5 requires four things at once; section 16's last line says 'Phase 0 exits when this command exits 0'. Two of section 5's four parts depend on instruments that do not exist (surface-probe.mjs's OPS-24 legs, P-197, whose cost meter is carded 'not built' and which A-150 records as having zero OPS-24 predicates) or are blocked (P-210's coverage enumeration, A-178). The instrument's own self-test 6 enshrines the blindness: an R-2 rail excluded 'does not open anything', so a buildable-area figure leaking on the map/PE payload and disclosure strings is invisible to a store read. FALSE_EARNED holds three predicates, two of them on the SAME rail (setbackFrontFt), while the false-absence writers (parcel-setback-cells.mjs buildNoRuledTableCells / buildResolvedCells) write every setback rail; the third predicate (ag-valuation-no-source) reads 0 by construction.

Nine of the fifteen real L-E customer-experience defects and seven of the eleven X-items have NO OWNING ROW: D2 (Waco panel declines what its own endpoint draws), D5, D6, D7 (Williamson, no MCP snapshot and no composed address, A-179's own 'new', uncarded), D8, D9, D11, D12 (salesHistory absent from the MCP schema -- P-209 is the ruling, not the schema fix), D14's resolution; and X2, X4, X5, X6, X8, X9, X11. The scope also uses 'D' for TWO different lists, so 'map D1 to D16' is ambiguous by construction (X5's parenthetical cites L-E's D2 = Waco, while section 4.5's D2 = P-217). Give L-E's list its own prefix. And section 4.5b's own standard -- fifteen buckets and the PDF leg graded before Phase 0 exits -- is not in section 5's exit.

ADD-084 is the one security debt that blocks Burnet, and it blocks by program law rather than by judgement: the exposed PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL is the read-write credential for the store Burnet's stage 10 publishes to, it is still at version 1 (2026-08-28) twelve days after exposure, rotation touches nine secrets across two projects plus every consumer's redeploy, and law 4 makes a write to a production serving store one of exactly three operator stop points. Card the ROTATION, not the incident. Separately: section 4.6 C5's instruction to 'add it to secret-rotation.mjs' is under-specified and would be implemented as a no-op -- ROTATION_TARGETS is Object.freeze'd with exactly two keys and rotateStagingSecrets reads branchRecords[key] and projectIds[key], so a third target needs a third frozen entry AND a third branchRecords entry from staging-reset AND a third projectIds entry.

The FAN-DEPTH commit gate does not fire in the harness this dispatch was handed to. .claude/settings.json registers fan-depth-gate.mjs commit under a Claude Code PreToolUse/Bash matcher, there is no .git/hooks/pre-commit in this worktree and core.hooksPath is empty, and A-181's own named-bypass list includes 'Cursor and any harness that does not load .claude/hooks' and 'commits made outside Claude Code'. The dispatch's sentence 'The commit gate refuses a close that declares any (A-181)' is therefore not enforced here; my subAgents declaration is honest, not enforced. Card a real pre-commit hook.

Two missing instruments are on the critical path to Burnet and no row owns either: the RE-COUNT of txgio_address for 48053 immediately before the run (A-150a's named precondition; the 2026-08-08 measurement had Burnet absent, and the Find box resolves through that table, so no surface-probe lookup can pass in Burnet regardless of pipeline quality), and the reconciliation of Burnet's 59,785 production parcels against 50,138 geometry-ingest features, which the scope's own document says 'nobody reconciled' -- under the register's A3-2 check Burnet could not proceed past stage 3.

The critical path to Burnet is not P-201 or P-249. S1 deliberately turns the setback rails red in all six counties ('The gate then REFUSES setbacks with a count, in every county. That is the honest state.'), and six-county-completeness.classify marks refuse OPEN on a must-pass rail (self-test 9). So section 5's exit is unreachable until S3 clears BOTH halves of 219,472 parcels -- 54 cities' zoning layers and tables plus 172 uncoded district codes across ~10 wired cities. Section 13 item 6 says only that farm MACHINERY builds in parallel; the Burnet RUN waits. Put that sentence in section 12.
